Simulate a steady-state, two-phase (oil–water) flow in a horizontal pipe using the OpenFOAM solver twoPhaseEulerFoam.
The pipe has an internal diameter of 0.05 m and a length of 1.0 m (L/D = 20), oriented horizontally along the x-axis.
At the inlet boundary, impose a uniform fixed mixture velocity U = (1.0 0 0) m/s.
At the inlet boundary, set alpha.water as fixedValue uniform 0.3.
At the pipe walls, apply noSlip condition for all velocity fields.
At the outlet boundary in 0/alpha.water, set type zeroGradient (no fixed alpha value at the outlet).
At the outlet boundary for velocity fields, apply zeroGradient to allow the developed profile to exit unimpeded.
Use water properties: rho = 998 kg/m³, mu = 0.001 Pa·s.
Use oil properties: rho = 850 kg/m³, mu = 0.003 Pa·s.
Generate a structured mesh (blockMesh or equivalent) with approximately 100 axial cells, 20 radial cells, and 40 circumferential cells, with near-wall refinement (y+ in the range 30–60 for the water phase).
Use the SIMPLE algorithm for pressure-velocity coupling with alpha.water transported via an MULES or equivalent bounded scheme.
Enable an incompressible two-phase Eulerian solver configuration with interfacial drag closure (Tomiyama or Schiller-Naumann) and interfacial area transport.
Apply a standard k-epsilon or k-omega SST turbulence model for both phases with particle-turbulence interaction (Saffman lift or similar).
Run the simulation in steady-state mode with convergence targets: residuals below 1e-5 for U, p, and alpha.water, and a monitor on alpha.water at the outlet cross-section showing less than 0.1% change over 20 consecutive iterations.
All solver and discretization settings (grad, div, laplacian schemes) follow standard OpenFOAM second-order central differencing for convection terms in a steady-state two-phase context.
